*   **Limitations:** 3D texture access is slower than 2D; fill rate limited; pre-processing cost for transfer function changes; image quality can suffer from banding if 2D textures are used instead of 3D [S4].

The claim lists four specific limitations: 1) 3D texture access is slower than 2D, 2) fill rate is limited, 3) pre-processing cost for transfer function changes, and 4) image quality suffers from banding if 2D textures are used instead of 3D. All four points are explicitly supported by Source [S4]: - '3D texture access is slower than 2D' is supported by the passage stating 'accesos a texturas tridimensionales son más lentos que los accesos a texturas bidimensionales'. - 'Fill rate limited' is supported by 'el algoritmo está limitado principalmente por el fill rate'. - 'Pre-processing cost' is supported by the discussion on pre-classification vs post-classification, where pre-classification involves applying the transfer function to all samples before interpolation ('pre-clasificación... se toma la muestra de un voxel y se le aplica la función de transferencia... Hecho esto para todas las muestras'), implying a computational cost/cost for changes compared to post-classification. - 'Image quality can suffer from banding if 2D textures are used instead of 3D' is supported by '3D textures provide superior image quality compared to 2D textures because they use trilinear interpolation, whereas 2D textures use bilinear interpolation which causes banding artifacts.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The mention of 'hardware-accelerated' is supported by [S1]'s reference to 'hardware' in the context of the technique and [S2]'s discussion of hardware lookups and vertex programs.
